```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(wikibaser)
```

## Retrieving entities from Wikibase

Wikidata is a collaboratively edited knowledge base built on Wikibase.
Other Wikimedia projects and independent organisations can also operate
Wikibase repositories with their own items, properties and identifiers.

An item is identified by a QID, such as [Q42](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q42)
(Douglas Adams), and a property by a PID, such as
[P31](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Property:P31) (instance of).
An entity can have multilingual labels, descriptions and aliases, as well
as statements. Items can also have sitelinks to pages on other wikis.

The `wb_get_entity()` function is an R wrapper around the MediaWiki
Action API module [`wbgetentities`](https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=help&modules=wbgetentities).
Although the API module supports retrieving multiple entities, this R
function retrieves one item or property at a time. By default, it uses
Wikidata; authenticated sessions can be used with other Wikibase repositories.

## A reproducible copy of Q42

Wikidata is continuously edited. Retrieving the same QID on different days
may therefore return different labels, statements or references.
To make the examples reproducible, wikibaser includes a saved API response
for Q42 in its example data.

```{r fixture}
cache_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "wikidata-cache", package = "wikibaser", mustWork = TRUE
)
fixture_file <- file.path(cache_path, "Q42.json")
fixture_date <- as.Date(file.info(fixture_file)$mtime, tz = "UTC")
fixture_date
```

The bundled response has a file modification date of **`r format(fixture_date, "%d %B %Y")`**
(UTC). This is the recorded date of the local file, not necessarily the
original retrieval date: installation or copying may change file timestamps.
The saved entity may no longer be fully in sync with live Wikidata.

```{r cache}
cache <- wb_entity_cache(path = cache_path, max_age_hours = Inf)
entity <- wb_get_entity("Q42", cache = cache, policy = "cache-only")
```

The `cache-only` policy reads the saved response without contacting Wikidata.
The infinite maximum cache age is appropriate for a fixed historical fixture.
For ordinary working caches, a finite maximum age may be more appropriate.

The saved response also contains the entity's revision identifier and last
modification timestamp. These describe the saved Wikidata revision, rather
than the date on which the local file was written.

```{r revision}
entity$id
entity$lastrevid
entity$modified
```

## Inspecting the saved entity

The default result is an R list representing the entity returned by the API.

```{r entity}
names(entity)
entity$labels$mul
entity$claims$P31
```

The language code `mul` denotes a default label used across languages.
It is not an English (`en`) label, and should not be silently treated as one.

The original API response can also be retrieved as a JSON file.

```{r json}
json_file <- wb_get_entity(
  "Q42", cache = cache, policy = "cache-only", as = "json"
)
file.exists(json_file)
```

This file is a separate temporary copy of the complete API response,
including the response envelope. The bundled fixture remains unchanged.

## Labels, descriptions and aliases

Labels identify an entity for human readers, descriptions help distinguish
it from similarly named entities, and aliases provide alternative names.
The `wb_entity_description()` function represents these multilingual terms
as a tibble.

```{r descriptions}
descriptions <- wb_entity_description("Q42", cache = cache)
head(descriptions)
```

In the default long format, each row represents an entity and a language.
Multiple aliases in the same language are separated by ` | `.
Missing terms are represented by `NA`.

We can select particular languages without introducing translations or
substituting labels from another language.

```{r languages}
languages <- c("mul", "az", "en", "hu")
selected <- wb_entity_description(
  "Q42", cache = cache, languages = languages
)
selected
```

For a directory of entities, a wide representation is often more convenient.
Each language-specific term becomes a separate variable.

```{r wide}
wide <- wb_entity_description(
  "Q42", cache = cache, languages = languages, format = "wide"
)
wide
```

Requested languages with no descriptive metadata are omitted. A language
with a description but no label is retained, with a missing label value.
The description wrapper uses the default `prefer-cache` retrieval policy.
With the bundled response and infinite cache age, these examples normally
read from the local cache without making an API request.

## Selecting statement values

A Wikibase statement consists of a main snak and may also have qualifiers,
references and a rank. The main snak associates a property with a value,
or indicates that the value is unknown or that there is no value.

For a directory, we may need only selected main-snak values, rather than
all the information contained in each statement. Here we select
P31 (instance of) and P106 (occupation) from the saved entity.

```{r statements}
properties <- c("P31", "P106")
values <- lapply(properties, function(property) {
  statements <- entity$claims[[property]]
  values <- vapply(statements, function(statement) {
    if (identical(statement$rank, "deprecated")) {
      return(NA_character_)
    }
    value <- statement$mainsnak$datavalue$value$id
    if (is.null(value)) NA_character_ else value
  }, FUN.VALUE = character(1))
  values <- values[!is.na(values)]
  if (length(values)) paste(values, collapse = " | ") else NA_character_
})
names(values) <- properties
values
```

This example is deliberately limited to item-valued properties. The values
are QIDs, not labels. Multiple values are retained in their returned order,
separated by ` | `. Deprecated statements and statements without a concrete
item value are excluded. Both normal and preferred ranks are retained.

We can add these selected values to the wide descriptive record and rename
the properties for human readers.

```{r directory}
directory <- wide
directory$instance_of <- values$P31
directory$occupation <- values$P106
directory
```

The package also provides `wb_entity_assertions()` for tabular extraction
of main-snak values across properties, with collapsed or widened multiple
values. The explicit extraction above works directly with the saved entity
and does not require another retrieval. A flattened directory is a derived
representation, not a replacement for the original Wikibase statements:
qualifiers, references, ranks and statement identifiers are not preserved
in these columns.

## Validating reproducible results

A saved API response allows us to check that a transformation produces the
expected result for a known input. For example, the bundled Q42 response
contains the default label Douglas Adams and an instance-of value Q5
(human).

```{r validate}
stopifnot(
  identical(entity$id, "Q42"),
  identical(wide$label_mul, "Douglas Adams"),
  "Q5" %in% strsplit(values$P31, " | ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
)
```

We can also check that the JSON output preserves the original API response
byte for byte.

```{r validate-json}
stopifnot(identical(
  readBin(fixture_file, "raw", n = file.info(fixture_file)$size),
  readBin(json_file, "raw", n = file.info(json_file)$size)
))
unlink(json_file)
```

These checks validate the retrieval and transformation of the saved data.
They do not establish that the statements are true, complete or still
current on Wikidata. Evaluating their sources and meaning remains a separate
review task.

## Working with live repositories

For live Wikidata retrieval, use the same wrapper without a cache, or create
a separate working cache. The following examples are not evaluated when
building this vignette.

```{r live, eval=FALSE}
current_entity <- wb_get_entity("Q42")
working_cache <- wb_entity_cache(max_age_hours = 24)
current_entity <- wb_get_entity(
  "Q42", cache = working_cache, policy = "prefer-api"
)
```

A working cache can be refreshed as the repository changes. The bundled
fixture should instead be treated as read-only, so that examples and tests
continue to refer to the same saved revision.
